articles.title: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
articles.titleEn: The Virtual Biotech: A multi-agent AI framework for therapeutic discovery and development
articles.abstract: Drug development requires evidence integration across biological scales and modalities, but relevant tools are fragmented. We introduce the Virtual Biotech, an organization of artificial intelligence (AI) agents modeled on a drug-development company, with agentic divisions spanning target discovery, safety assessment, modality selection, and clinical development. We demonstrate its utility at three drug-development decision points. First, more than 37,000 agents annotated outcomes from 55,984 trials and found that drugs targeting cell type–specific genes were 48% more likely to reach market with 32% fewer adverse events. Second, it integrated multimodal evidence to propose a therapeutic strategy in lung cancer. Third, it analyzed a terminated ulcerative colitis trial and inferred potential mechanisms of failure. These results demonstrate that human-guided multi-agent systems can conduct transparent, multiscale analyses to inform therapeutic-development decisions.

articles.title: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
articles.titleEn: Safeguarding global terrestrial vertebrate species from future sea level rise
articles.abstract: Sea level rise (SLR) threatens terrestrial biodiversity, yet its spatiotemporal and species-specific impacts remain unclear. Integrating relative SLR projections across five shared socioeconomic pathways (SSPs) with area of habitat (AOH) maps for 34,120 terrestrial vertebrate species, we project that species exposed to SLR will increase from up to 13,680 in 2050 to 15,324 by 2100, including 57 to 63% of birds, 47 to 52% of mammals, 28 to 36% of reptiles, and 20 to 24% of amphibians. In Southeast Asia, inland inundation areas support high richness. Under SSP5-8.5, species facing >10% habitat inundation surge from 18 in 2050 to 109 by 2100, with reptiles and already threatened species overrepresented. Safeguarding SLR refugia—the noninundated habitats for exposed species—is critical, yet more than 96% lie outside protected areas, which means that early international action is required.

articles.title: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.titleEn: Late Holocene reexpansion of the Laurentide Ice Sheet
articles.abstract: During interglaciations, the Laurentide Ice Sheet (LIS), which is the largest of the Pleistocene ice sheets, retreats to Arctic Canada, where it achieves a minimum configuration. The reexpansion of the LIS following this minimum marks the start of the next glaciation. Here, we show that the last remaining remnant of the most recent LIS, Barnes Ice Cap (Baffin Island, Canada), achieved its minimum interglacial dimensions after ~3.6 thousand years ago, before reexpanding ~2000 years ago, marking the onset of the next glaciation. The new LIS reached maximum dimensions in ~1960 CE, after which anthropogenic summer warming resulted in a negative mass balance, ice margin recession, and the termination of the next glaciation. The demise of the next glaciation, despite the ongoing decline in summer insolation, illustrates the influence of anomalous greenhouse gas forcing on climate.

articles.title: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.titleEn: Thermodynamic origin of the phonon Hall effect in a honeycomb antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: The underlying mechanism of the thermal Hall effect generated by phonons in a variety of insulators is yet to be identified. In this work, we report on a sizable thermal Hall conductivity in nickel phosphorus trisulfide (NiPS 3 ), a van der Waals stack of honeycomb layers with a zigzag antiferromagnetic order. The longitudinal (κ aa ) and the transverse (κ ab ) thermal conductivities peak at the same temperature, and the thermal Hall angle, at this peak, respects a previously identified bound. The amplitude of κ ab is extremely sensitive to the amplitude of magnetization along the b axis but is not correlated with the phonon mean free path, which points to an intrinsic origin.

articles.title: The AI debate is missing half the system
articles.titleEn: The AI debate is missing half the system
articles.abstract: Last month, leading executives of artificial intelligence (AI) companies warned the United Nations Security Council about the risks of losing human control over this rapidly advancing technology. Their recommendations focused heavily on safeguards, evaluation, and governance of AI models and systems, largely overlooking the risks that arise from the interactions of AI with people and institutions. AI safety needs to be addressed at the level of the human–AI system, not the AI model alone.

articles.title: Sequential diagnosis with language models
articles.titleEn: Sequential diagnosis with language models
articles.abstract: We explored the capabilities of frontier language models in sequential diagnosis, a diagnostic paradigm that captures the iterative nature of clinical reasoning. Given a brief clinical presentation, clinicians selectively acquired information to reach a diagnosis, enabling assessment of diagnostic accuracy and workup cost. We developed an interactive benchmark and an artificial intelligence (AI) system that simulates a panel of physicians, continually revising the differential diagnosis and selecting cost-effective tests. Using this benchmark, the system achieved 83.2% accuracy on New England Journal of Medicine clinicopathological conference cases and 80.3% on MIMIC-IV-ED emergency department admissions, outperforming generalist physicians (36.1 and 46.8%, respectively). Although these findings were obtained in a controlled benchmark setting, they highlight the promise of language models for supporting more accurate, lower-cost diagnoses.

articles.title: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.titleEn: Dynamic functionality–enabled fast and selective transport in nanochannels
articles.abstract: Nanochannels capable of fast and selective mass transport are central to applications in energy, resources, biomedicine, and the environment. However, extreme nanoscale confinement, often coupled with rigid channel environments, imposes substantial frictional and adhesive barriers, causing sluggish transport and constrained selectivity. We identified nanochannel dynamics as a key to addressing these challenges by harnessing the intrinsic mobility (e.g., self-rotation) of confined functionalities to enhance molecular transport. Through a combination of experiments and simulations, we demonstrated that such dynamics reshape transport by promoting kinetic energy transfer and enabling more efficient molecular relays, thereby improving separation performance beyond current benchmarks. Our findings highlight the role of nanochannel dynamics in regulating mass transport under confinement and provide a framework for designing advanced nanochannel systems.

articles.title: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
articles.titleEn: Superlubricity by glycerosome boundary layers
articles.abstract: The search for high-performance lubricants is of broad relevance to biomedical applications, including artificial joints, regenerative scaffolds, and osteoarthritis therapies. Here we introduce glycerosomes—phosphatidylcholine (PC)-based vesicles containing glycerol—as a promising boundary lubricant. Using a surface force balance, we show that glycerosomes achieve a friction coefficient as low as 10 − 5 under a high compression pressure of 15.6 MPa, representing a 20-fold reduction compared to conventional PC liposomes. This level of lubrication surpasses any previously reported boundary lubricant system at such pressures in aqueous media. Mechanistically, glycerosomes exhibit substantially lower adhesion energy than PC liposomes, and theoretical simulations reveal enhanced vesicle stability and flexibility. Our findings establish glycerosomes as a superior hydration lubrication platform, with promising implications for both biomedical implants and industrial applications requiring robust lubricity.

articles.title: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
articles.titleEn: Virus transmission required for maintenance and host adaptation mirrors neurophysiological differences in rabies-derived peptides
articles.abstract: Pathogen adaptations to new hosts are central to the disease ecology of cross-species transmission and host switching of viruses. The rabies virus is a model for adaptations to different hosts as it induces behavioral changes that facilitate transmission, while being maintained in distinct species-specific cycles of infection. Here, we demonstrate that the rabies virus requires distinct transmission dynamics in two hosts with different ecologies to establish maintenance, using agent-based modeling, analyses of virus glycoprotein-mediated manipulation of neuroreceptor function, and phylogenetic analysis. Epidemiological models suggest that rabies virus variants adapted to arctic foxes, which sustain rabies virus at very low host densities, require a higher probability of transmission than viruses adapted to raccoons. Using in vitro electrophysiology, we demonstrate that the rabies glycoprotein-derived peptides from arctic fox rabies variants are more potent antagonists of alpha7 nicotinic acetylcholine receptors. These findings suggest a possible functional basis for the behavioral modifications that drive enzootic rabies transmission in the context of host ecology. In addition, a large proportion of residues that may drive rabies virus adaptation to raccoons and arctic foxes are found within this neurotoxin-like region. Furthermore, a residue in the neurotoxin-like region of the mature rabies virus glycoprotein (residue 183) has been associated with pathogenicity, host switching, and disease ecology in previous studies. We propose the hypothesis that rabies virus transmission dynamics adapt to the ecology and physiology of novel hosts through the selection of glycoproteins that elicit specific degrees of behavioral modification and transmission probability.

articles.title: Exploring Climate Change Effects on Concurrent Floods and Concurrent Droughts via Statistical Deep Learning
articles.titleEn: Exploring Climate Change Effects on Concurrent Floods and Concurrent Droughts via Statistical Deep Learning
articles.abstract: Concurrent floods and concurrent droughts in nearby catchments pose challenges to risk assessment and water management. Climate change is affecting extremely high and low discharge, but the complex interplay between changes in individual catchments, and in the dependence across catchments, make it difficult to provide accurate assessments of the occurrence probabilities of concurrent extremes. In this work, we use a contemporary statistical deep learning model to capture concurrent river floods and droughts in four catchments in the Upper Danube basin, based on discharge simulated by a hydrological model driven with large ensemble climate model output. The statistical model is able to accurately capture the tail behavior of the simulated discharge, which we assess by making use of the large available sample. We subsequently use our statistical model to study changes in joint tail behavior of discharge over time, finding that both compound flooding and drought‐like conditions are becoming increasingly likely toward the end of the 21st century under a high‐emission scenario. In particular, our results highlight that changes in the dependence structure of extremes strongly contribute to the detected changes, an aspect that would be difficult to capture with traditional approaches. This work paves the way for highly flexible, general inference on compound extremes in hydrological applications, and demonstrates key advantages of using statistical deep learning in this setting.

articles.title: Analysis of Dual‐Porosity Model With Fissure Skin Effect in Confined Karst Aquifer
articles.titleEn: Analysis of Dual‐Porosity Model With Fissure Skin Effect in Confined Karst Aquifer
articles.abstract: In fractured media with rough fissure skins, ignoring the fissure skin effect limits the accuracy of parameter inversion. In karst aquifers, groundwater storage and movement are typically governed by dual‐porosity models, where the fissure skin plays a key role in water exchange between fissures and the rock matrix. This study develops a radial CRT model incorporating the fissure skin effect based on a quasi‐steady state approach, deriving an analytical solution in the Laplace domain and obtaining a real‐time domain solution via Stehfest method. articles.title: Four Decades of Reach‐Scale Declines in Total Phosphorus Across the Yellow River Basin Driven by Vegetation Restoration and Dam Impoundment
articles.titleEn: Four Decades of Reach‐Scale Declines in Total Phosphorus Across the Yellow River Basin Driven by Vegetation Restoration and Dam Impoundment
articles.abstract: Phosphorus (P) is a finite resource fundamental to terrestrial and aquatic productivity. However, excessive P transfer from land to rivers threatens food production and degrades water quality. Systematic analyses of multidecadal total phosphorus (TP) variation in large river basins remain challenging because of incomplete and non‐uniform observational data. Here, we develop a potentially transferable and generalizable framework combining remote sensing and machine learning to reconstruct long‐term and reach‐scale TP variation in the Yellow River Basin from 1986 to 2024, based on synchronous multimodal and in situ data ( N = 1,490). The results confirm that the framework can reliably estimate TP concentration, achieving Nash–Sutcliffe efficiency = 0.71 and root mean squared error = 27.1 μg L −1 on the test set. TP concentration shows a significant temporal decline in 55% of river reaches; spatial heterogeneity is evident, with concentrations in the middle reaches declining most rapidly at 4.1 μg L −1 per decade. However, TP flux (TPF) exhibits a U‐shaped temporal trajectory, increasing after 2015 as river discharge rises; the spatial gradient follows a hump‐shaped pattern, characterized by a peak of 2,094 t yr −1 at Tongguan. Vegetation restoration reduces land‐to‐river TP export, and dam impoundment impedes in‐stream TP transport, both of which largely account for the declines in TP concentration in the Yellow River Basin. This study proposes a potentially generalizable framework for riverine TP reconstruction at high spatial resolution over multiple decades and provides new insights into the anthropogenic impact on TP dynamics in big river systems.

articles.title: Auto‐STIV: A Deep Learning Framework for Fully Autonomous Two‐Dimensional Streamflow Velocity Vector Field Estimation
articles.titleEn: Auto‐STIV: A Deep Learning Framework for Fully Autonomous Two‐Dimensional Streamflow Velocity Vector Field Estimation
articles.abstract: Accurate and continuous streamflow monitoring can support effective water resource management, yet substantial gaps persist in national streamgage networks due to operational challenges and costs. Non‐contact, image‐based techniques such as Space‐Time Image Velocimetry (STIV) offer a safe, scalable and, cost‐effective alternative for measuring surface flow velocity in rivers, which allows for streamflow calculation, especially during hazardous flood events. Traditional STIV methods, however, often require manual parameter tuning and struggle with complex flow conditions. This study introduces Auto‐STIV, a novel deep learning framework that fully automates the estimation of both flow direction and velocity magnitude from video imagery. The proposed approach utilizes a two‐stage Convolutional Neural Network model. The first stage predicts the primary flow direction by analyzing a stack of Space‐Time Images (STIs) generated from a series of candidate orientations. The second stage estimates the velocity magnitude from the STI corresponding to the predicted direction. The model was trained on a comprehensive data set collected under diverse, controlled laboratory conditions and evaluated using real‐world footage from the Colorado River. Results demonstrate that Auto‐STIV outperforms the traditional autocorrelation‐based STIV method, exhibiting higher accuracy and greater robustness in the presence of challenging environmental factors such as variable lighting, low‐contrast surface textures, and complex flow patterns. This research underscores the potential of deep learning to enhance the capabilities of image‐based velocimetry, that may support more reliable, scalable, and automated streamflow monitoring systems.

articles.title: A data-driven method coupling multiple physical constraints for correcting structural errors in groundwater contaminant transport models
articles.titleEn: A data-driven method coupling multiple physical constraints for correcting structural errors in groundwater contaminant transport models
articles.abstract: Model structural errors are pervasive in groundwater contaminant transport modeling under complex environmental conditions, hindering accurate prediction of contamination transport. Data-driven methods (DDMs) coupled with physical constraints provide an effective approach for correcting structural errors and improving prediction. However, in multicomponent reactive transport systems, multiple physical mechanisms must be satisfied simultaneously, whereas existing DDMs have limited capacity to effectively couple multiple physical constraints. To address this challenge, this study proposes a general method for correcting structural errors in groundwater models. A combined likelihood function is constructed and sub-likelihood weights are dynamically updated to effectively couple multiple physical constraints. The method is evaluated using a synthetic three-dimensional tetrachloroethylene reactive transport simulation and a cadmium-phosphate cotransport sand column experiment. These tests systematically assess the effects of coupling single versus multiple physical constraints on structural error correction and predictive performance. The results show that coupling multiple constraints can constrain parameter identification, reduce predictive uncertainty, and more comprehensively improve model predictions. Appropriate physical constraints function analogously to incorporating additional observations. Moreover, coupling multiple physical constraints results in a simpler form of structural error in the calibrated groundwater model, making it easier to characterize, thereby enhancing prediction accuracy and physical consistency. The proposed dynamic updating and stopping criterion of sub-likelihood weights maintains a balance between multiple physical constraints and observations, improving the robustness of parameter identification and constraint enforcement. Overall, the proposed DDM coupled with multiple physical constraints provides a general framework for correcting structural errors in complex groundwater contaminant transport models.

articles.title: Benchmarking convection-permitting climate simulations for hydrometeorological characterizations: a comparative study of WRF-SAAG and observation-based products in Chile
articles.titleEn: Benchmarking convection-permitting climate simulations for hydrometeorological characterizations: a comparative study of WRF-SAAG and observation-based products in Chile
articles.abstract: Over the last few years, significant progress has been made in the development of convection-permitting climate models (CPCMs), especially in improving precipitation estimates in regions with complex terrain. Recently, the South American Affinity Group (SAAG) developed a novel high-resolution dataset – hereafter referred to as the WRF-SAAG dataset – by dynamically downscaling the ERA5 reanalysis using the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model over South America for the period 2000–2021. Here, we evaluate WRF-SAAG outputs across continental Chile and compare them with two widely used gridded meteorological products, CR2MET and RF-MEP, which combine reanalysis data with in situ measurements. In particular, we analyze spatial differences among climatological estimates from the three products, and we assess the quality of daily precipitation and daily maximum and minimum temperature simulations using observations from meteorological stations over the period April/2001–March/2018. We also compare the potential of these climate datasets for hydrological modeling using a conceptual, bucket-style rainfall-runoff model, evaluating the results against streamflow observations, satellite remote sensing (SRS) products, and a snow water equivalent (SWE) reanalysis product. We found that the detection accuracy varied within each Chilean macrozone, with worse performance in the Far North (17.5–26° S) and Patagonia (43.7–56° S). The evaluation of daily precipitation against station observations using Tang's Kling–Gupta efficiency (KGE T ) reveals that all datasets performed better in reproducing precipitation in rainy regions (median KGE T ≥ 0.65 in the Southern macrozone), while in arid areas such as the Near North during summer, the median KGE T was negative. The CR2MET product consistently provided the best performance for extreme precipitation and temperature, partly because it includes information from the stations used for evaluation. Finally, the application of the hydrological model shows that although WRF-SAAG simulations achieved runoff estimations comparable to the best observation-based gridded products (i.e., CR2MET or RF-MEP), with the best results in the southern macrozone they provided relatively lower performance in evapotranspiration (ET) and soil moisture estimates, as well as SWE simulations of competitive quality. More broadly, the results presented here show that, despite some remaining challenges in arid climate regions, kilometer-scale climate models can deliver valuable information for hydrological applications at the daily time scale in Chile.

In particular, we analyze spatial differences among climatological estimates from the three products, and we assess the quality of daily precipitation and daily maximum and minimum temperature simulations using observations from meteorological stations over the period April/2001–March/2018. articles.title: Evaluation of SWOT HR PIXC version D water level time series of small lakes
articles.titleEn: Evaluation of SWOT HR PIXC version D water level time series of small lakes
articles.abstract: The Surface Water and Ocean Topography (SWOT) satellite mission introduces unprecedented 2-D radar interferometry to inland hydrology, aiming to evaluate water bodies down to 0.0625 km 2 . Standard operational products, such as LakeSP, are designed for global applicability but may exhibit suboptimal design choices for particular hydrological regimes. To address this, a customized processing workflow utilizing low-level SWOT L2 HR PIXC vD data was evaluated using 37 small Danish lakes (0.25 to 40 km 2 ) against daily in-situ gauge data from July 2023 to May 2026. The workflow achieves a median root-mean-square error (RMSE) of 5.57 cm and a Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.91, similar to LakeSP. Crucially, this approach retains a median of 125 valid timestamps per lake compared to 60 timestamps preserved by the filtered LakeSP product, effectively doubling the temporal resolution and enabling the capture of higher-frequency hydrological variations. Additionally, we find indications that SWOT's PIXC data contains time-varying residual roll-errors over Danish lakes that affect ca 18 % of all passes with more than 10 observed lakes covering Denmark.

articles.title: Optimization of the fast layer transmittance algorithm in RTTOV v13.1 for strong water vapor absorption channels of the FY-3F HIRAS-II instrument using LBLRTM v12.11
articles.titleEn: Optimization of the fast layer transmittance algorithm in RTTOV v13.1 for strong water vapor absorption channels of the FY-3F HIRAS-II instrument using LBLRTM v12.11
articles.abstract: Fast and accurate calculation of atmospheric transmittance is essential for infrared atmospheric remote sensing and satellite data assimilation. However, fast radiative transfer models show significant errors in strong water vapor absorption channels (e.g., near 6.7 µm). An important reason is the numerical instability encountered during the regression of transmittance coefficients when dealing with lower and middle atmosphere. To address this, this study proposes an optimized scheme to calculate atmospheric transmittance vertical profiles for the RTTOV (Radiative Transfer for TOVS) fast transmittance algorithm. The method introduces a physically motivated transmittance threshold to sub-select training samples and employs a cumulative transmittance-based weighting factor within a weighted least squares regression to recalibrate the transmittance coefficients. It aims to optimize the calculation scheme for transmittance coefficients of the Hyperspectral Infrared Atmospheric Sounder-II (HIRAS-II) instrument onboard the Fengyun-3F satellite (FY-3F). The method is assessed by calculations on the training profile datasets provided within the RTTOV model framework. By comparing transmittance and brightness temperature calculations at 6.7 µm from this method with those from a line-by-line model and observations from HIRAS-II, the results show that the accuracy of the forward model for the 6.7 µm absorption channel is significantly enhanced by applying a threshold-based noise reduction method. This improvement enhances the stability and reliability of the transmittance calculations for this strong absorption band. Further accuracy enhancements are obtained by incorporating weighting corrections into the calculations of transmittance coefficients. The root mean square error (RMSE) and bias of the observation minus background (OMB) time series for FY-3F HIRAS-II demonstrate that the transmittance coefficient calculation scheme with weighting factor correction improves the forward model accuracy, which is more consistent with RTTOV simulation results. The mean OMB bias at the 6.7 µm absorption-peak channel is closer to zero than that of RTTOV, whereas the OMB biases at the channels on either side of the absorption peak remain consistent with those of RTTOV.

articles.title: Hydromorphological Restoration of Streams Does Not Ensure the Recovery of Ecosystem Functioning
articles.titleEn: Hydromorphological Restoration of Streams Does Not Ensure the Recovery of Ecosystem Functioning
articles.abstract: Ecological restoration is widely expected to recover multiple ecosystem attributes, yet biological structure and ecosystem functioning may respond differently to hydromorphological restoration. Interpreting functional change is further complicated because higher or lower process rates do not inherently indicate recovery; their ecological meaning depends on how degraded and restored conditions compare with an appropriate reference state. We synthesised 582 effect sizes from 66 studies to quantify responses of nine ecosystem functions to hydromorphological restoration of streams and to assess whether changes in biological structure coincided with functional responses. Ecosystem‐function responses varied substantially among processes and baselines. Gross primary production was significantly higher in degraded than in reference streams, illustrating that elevated functional rates do not necessarily indicate reference‐like ecological conditions. Restoration did not consistently reverse degradation‐associated functional differences: denitrification was significantly lower in restored than in degraded streams, whereas nitrate uptake remained significantly lower in restored than in reference streams. Other restored–reference differences were generally weak or uncertain. Functional responses did not differ systematically among broad restoration‐measure categories. Restoration age was associated with changes in gross primary production and denitrification relative to degraded conditions, but none of the functions showed detectable convergence towards or divergence from reference conditions through time. In studies measuring both biological structure and ecosystem functioning, biological responses to restoration were generally positive relative to degraded conditions, whereas functional responses were more variable. However, the available evidence was too uncertain to conclude that biological and functional responses systematically differed. Our synthesis shows that functional recovery cannot be inferred either from restoration‐associated change alone or from concurrent biological recovery. Assessing restoration success therefore requires direct measurements of ecosystem processes and ecologically meaningful reference conditions that reveal whether functional change represents movement towards a process‐specific restoration target.

articles.title: Non‐Linear Increases of Soil Carbon Stocks and Turnover Along Alpine Greening Gradients on Different Bedrocks
articles.titleEn: Non‐Linear Increases of Soil Carbon Stocks and Turnover Along Alpine Greening Gradients on Different Bedrocks
articles.abstract: Alpine ecosystems are experiencing warming, leading to alpine greening—an upward migration and enhanced productivity of vegetation. Although soils represent the largest carbon (C) stocks in these ecosystems, impacts of greening on soil organic carbon (SOC) dynamics remain unknown, especially in the high alpine zone. We measured SOC stocks, quality and radiocarbon ( 14 C) based turnover rates along elevation gradients from (sub)alpine forests to periglacial zones on three bedrock types, representing trajectories of changes in climate and vegetation and weathering regime. Data were linked to SOC stabilizing pedogenic oxides (PO) to assess the potential of soils to sequester C upon alpine greening. Results show pronounced decreases in SOC stocks (from 10 to 1 kg C m −2 ) and increases in 14 C‐based turnover times (from decades to millennia) with increasing elevation. This pattern followed a non‐linear sigmoidal function with a threshold at the vegetation line where grassland transitions to the nival zone. High alpine soils showed low SOC:PO ratios, indicating low C saturation and a high capacity to stabilize SOC on reactive minerals. However, negligible 14 C‐derived carbon inputs suggest that low vegetation productivity constrains SOC sequestration in these soils. In contrast, towards lower elevation with a warmer climate, grassland soils receive higher C inputs, but appear more C saturated, leading to greater SOC turnover but little SOC stock changes. Bedrock influenced SOC dynamics with approximately 50% smaller SOC stocks and faster turnover rates in dolomitic than in siliceous soils, due to slower weathering and lower SOC stabilization. Using elevation as a space‐for‐time substitution, we infer that SOC sequestration under alpine greening will be confined to areas around the vegetation line, with parent material influencing the magnitude of C uptake. Future projections of SOC dynamics should account for vegetation shifts and bedrock‐driven stabilization to constrain the role of alpine soils in land carbon‐climate feedbacks.

articles.title: Contrasting isotopic responses of dryland and wetland plants to a century of global anthropogenic changes in nutrient cycling
articles.titleEn: Contrasting isotopic responses of dryland and wetland plants to a century of global anthropogenic changes in nutrient cycling
articles.abstract: Anthropogenic emissions of carbon dioxide and reactive nitrogen in various forms disrupt the functioning of ecosystems around the world. In Europe, many valuable habitats, particularly wetlands and semi-natural dry grasslands, are under threat from ongoing eutrophication. However, due to contrasting water regimes, the uptake of anthropogenic nitrogen by plants in these ecosystems is different and is also interrelated with an increase in trophic level in both habitats. In our study, we measured the δ 15 N and δ 13 C values, as well as the total nitrogen content (TN), of 99 pairs of foliar samples collected from 14 species of vascular plants in Poland: seven wetland species and seven dry grassland species. Each pair consisted of a historical sample collected from a herbarium voucher dating from before 1939 (i.e. before artificial fertilisers were widely used in agriculture) and a contemporary sample collected in 2024 from the same species in a similar location. We performed t tests to determine whether there were significant differences in the means of δ 15 N, TN and δ 13 C between samples from the two different habitats. Next, we calculated the differences in δ 15 N, TN and δ 13 C between the contemporary and historical samples for each pair. Using the information on date of collection of each herbarium voucher we corrected δ 13 C values taking into consideration changes of atmospheric δ 13 C due to fossil-fuel combustion (so called Suess effect). We then tested whether the difference for each species and habitat type was significantly different from zero using 90 % confidence intervals. Using multiple linear regression, we analysed the relationships between differences in δ 15 N and TN over time and the following factors: habitat type, the proportion of farmland in the surrounding landscape, the consumption of synthetic nitrogen fertiliser, and NO x deposition. δ 15 N and TN values were lower in dry grassland species than in wetland species, in both the contemporary and historical subsets. For dry grassland species, the mean δ 15 N value was lower in contemporary samples than in historical ones. For wetland species, the opposite was true. The difference in δ 15 N values between pairs of samples was positively related to the amount of farmland in the surrounding landscape. The mean TN was higher in contemporary than in historical wetland plants, but not in dry grassland plants. The mean δ 13 C value, corrected for the Suess effect, was lower in contemporary samples than in historical ones. The mean difference was −0.51 ‰ for dry grassland and −3.85 ‰ for wetland species. Our study revealed that the century of fossil fuel-derived carbon emissions, increased nitrogen input into the environment, and dominance of artificial fertilisers and combustion-derived nitrogen over biological nitrogen sources have not led to consistent responses across habitats and species. While the isotopic composition of nitrogen and carbon in plant leaves in Central Europe has undoubtedly changed, this change is highly context-dependent. Its magnitude and direction are impacted by the type of habitat and the identity and/or ecology of the species. As expected, man-made alterations appear to be more pronounced in wetland environments than in dryland habitats. Furthermore, the source of disruption may differ between the two habitat types. Specifically, wetlands are exposed to a multitude of anthropogenic nitrogen and carbon sources, whereas dry grasslands seem to be predominantly affected by changes in the composition of the atmosphere.

articles.title: Temporal models for the occurrence of Etna eruptions and implications for hazard assessment
articles.titleEn: Temporal models for the occurrence of Etna eruptions and implications for hazard assessment
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: Mt. Etna volcanic activity is broadly divided into flank eruptions and summit paroxysms. Here, building on previously-available literature and data on the start time of these events, we collate two separate catalogs of the two activity types. Then we separately model their temporal occurrence. The catalog of flank eruptions, spanning the last 400 years, has been modelled by means of the most widely used renewal models, among which the best one (through Akaike Information Criterion) is the Brownian Passage Time. The catalog of summit paroxysms, covering the period 1986–2022, according to our cluster analysis is best characterized by 12 clusters of paroxysms. We separately analyze the inter-event times between onset times of successive clusters of paroxysms (Inter-Cluster inter-event times) and the inter-event times between successive paroxysms within clusters (Intra-Cluster inter-event times). Again, the Brownian Passage Time is the best-fitting model, obviously with very different parameters in the two cases. We test the best-fitting models by checking their ability to reproduce features of the real catalogs. Finally, we provide an example of how to use in practice such temporal models in the context of probabilistic hazard assessment, showing a possible use in the case of tephra fallout hazard from summit paroxysms. In particular, the proposed temporal model enables the assessment of probabilistic volcanic hazard for tephra fallout over different time windows accounting also for the uncertainty in the temporal occurrence of summit paroxysms.

articles.title: Distinguishing run-up height from pressure distribution during avalanche impact on narrow obstacles: mechanisms and semi-empirical prediction from three-dimensional simulations
articles.titleEn: Distinguishing run-up height from pressure distribution during avalanche impact on narrow obstacles: mechanisms and semi-empirical prediction from three-dimensional simulations
articles.journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
articles.abstract: In many avalanche engineering guidelines, run-up height is assumed to define the vertical extent of significant impact pressure of snow avalanches on narrow obstacles, such as cableway masts or transmission towers. Laboratory experiments indicate that this assumption is invalid in fast, inertia-driven regimes; however, the underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood, limiting the physical basis for improving design practice. To clarify these mechanisms and refine engineering formulations, we conduct a comprehensive numerical investigation using a three-dimensional Material Point Method, varying avalanche velocity and rheological parameters. Our results substantiate that run-up height and the vertical extent of significant impact pressure, which we term pressure height, are distinct quantities governed by different mechanisms. Both include a gravity-driven component controlled by avalanche rheology and independent of flow velocity. In fast flows, however, the two quantities diverge: run-up height gains a dominant inertia-driven component that scales with the square of the flow velocity, while avalanche rheology controls energy dissipation. Pressure height, by contrast, remains velocity-independent. This divergence arises from flow deflection at a dead zone near the obstacle base, where momentum is redirected and impact pressure concentrates. Building on these distinctions, we propose separate semi-empirical formulations for run-up height and pressure height. The run-up formulation follows the structure of the most common avalanche engineering guidelines, but replaces simplified avalanche-type classifications with a rheological parametrization. The pressure height relation adopts the same framework, while reflecting its distinct, velocity-independent governing mechanism.

articles.title: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
articles.titleEn: Tau isoform mapping across tissues and biofluids reveals a signature distinguishing Alzheimer’s disease from amyotrophic lateral sclerosis
articles.abstract: Blood phosphorylated tau 217 (p-tau217) accurately detects Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathology but is also elevated in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS), likely reflecting peripheral (big) tau released from muscle. Assays selectively measuring brain-derived (BD-) tau and BD-p-tau217 are therefore needed. We analysed serum BD-tau and p-tau217 in ALS ( n = 139), AD ( n = 101) and controls ( n = 75) using direct immunoassays and after BD-Tau immunoprecipitation (BD-Tau-IP), and tau species in brain ( n = 16), spinal cord ( n = 11) and muscle ( n = 10) by targeted mass spectrometry. With the direct immunoassays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in AD and ALS versus controls. After BD-Tau-IP, BD-tau and BD-p-tau217 were elevated in AD only, improving diagnostic accuracy. Mass spectrometry revealed a central-to-peripheral shift from BD-tau to big tau predominance, with exclusively big p-tau217 detected in muscle. Selective detection of BD-tau species improves the specificity of blood AD biomarkers by reducing peripheral tau confounding.

articles.title: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
articles.titleEn: Long-term electoral participation among Swedish survivors of the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami
articles.abstract: Natural disasters can spark demands for democratic accountability yet impose losses and displacement that depress participation. We study approximately 16,000 Swedish tourists exposed to the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami who returned home to intact communities. Unlike most people exposed to natural disasters, they faced no increase in the cost of voting, so the case is well suited to studying motivational responses to disaster exposure. We link a survivor registry to population-wide administrative data ( N up to 7 million) and use entropy balancing to compare survivors to matched non-exposed citizens over 25 years. Exposed individuals do not withdraw from participation. Their turnout is 1.4 percentage points higher in 2010 and 2018, a modest but persistent gap. The gap is more than twice as large among the bereaved. Mobilization is strongest among those exposed between ages 16 and 25, which is what habit formation would predict. A 2023 follow-up survey (3,956 respondents; N = 3198 to 3625 per analysis after item non-response) provides descriptive evidence that survivors still evaluate the government’s crisis response negatively and have shifted their partisan sympathies away from the then-incumbent party. The findings indicate that failed crisis management may have lasting consequences for turnout and potentially party choice, and that the electoral stakes of disaster response extend beyond the disaster zone.

articles.title: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
articles.titleEn: Trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease
articles.abstract: Gallstone disease is a highly prevalent and costly gastrointestinal disease. Yet, genetic variation in gallstone susceptibility and its implication in metabolic pathways remain to be explored. We report a trans-ancestry genome-wide association meta-analysis of gallstone disease including 100,856 cases and 1,596,602 controls in the UK Biobank, FinnGen, Biobank Japan, and Million Veteran Program. We identified 116 (59 novel) risk loci across meta-analysis and found replication in statistically compelling signals in the All of Us Research Program. A polygenic risk score constructed from trans-ancestry lead variants was positively associated with liver chemistry and alpha-1-antitrypsin deficiency and negatively associated with total cholesterol and low-density lipoprotein levels among trans-ancestry and European ancestry groups in the Penn Medicine BioBank. Colocalization of risk loci with 44 traits and with expression quantitative trait loci from eight tissues yielded 321 and 110 significant colocalizations, respectively. These findings broaden our understanding of the genetic architecture of gallstone disease.

articles.title: Reduced-DSP 200G/λ low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator enabled by built-in EO equalizer
articles.titleEn: Reduced-DSP 200G/λ low-voltage slow-light silicon modulator enabled by built-in EO equalizer
articles.abstract: Multi-Tb/s optical interconnects for artificial intelligence data centers necessitate high-speed, energy-efficient, and compact transceivers. However, conventional silicon Mach-Zehnder modulators are fundamentally limited by low modulation efficiency and large physical dimensions that typically extend several millimeters, requiring high-swing drivers and power-intensive digital signal processing to achieve data rates exceeding 100 Gb/s per lane. Here we show a silicon photonic crystal waveguide slow-light modulator that overcomes the bandwidth-efficiency trade-off via a built-in electro-optic equalizer. By monolithically integrating optical delay lines and crossings within segmented slow-light phase shifters, we synthesized an on-chip feedforward response that extends the 3-dB bandwidth. The fabricated modulator with a small device length of 320 µm demonstrated 140-Gb/s on-off keying operation with an energy consumption of 26 fJ/bit using drive voltages compatible with fin field-effect transistor-based complementary metal-oxide-semiconductor technology. Furthermore, four-level pulse amplitude modulation achieved 180 Gb/s without digital signal processing and 200 Gb/s with a low-complexity 11-tap digital equalizer. By reducing reliance on power-dissipating electronics, this strategy provides a potential route toward future dense multi-Tb/s co-packaged optics for energy-constrained switching systems.

articles.title: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
articles.titleEn: A van der Waals photon-ratchet for enhancing spin-defect emission and quantum sensing
articles.abstract: Spin defects in two-dimensional materials are promising platforms for quantum information technologies and nanoscale sensing. The negatively charged boron vacancy ( $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − ) in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) is particularly attractive due to its sensitivity to temperature, magnetic fields, and pressure, but its application is limited by intrinsically weak photoluminescence (PL). Here we demonstrate a van der Waals heterostructure that enhances the PL intensity of $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − by up to 45× at 4 Kelvin while preserving compatibility with ultrathin optoelectronic platforms. A quasi type-I band alignment at the PbI 2 –defected hBN interface facilitates efficient interlayer coupling to the defect, and strong spectral overlap supports fluorescence resonance energy transfer. Ab initio calculations indicate that this coupling enables a photon-ratcheting mechanism, in which optical absorption in PbI 2 generates a nonlinear polarization that drives $${\mathrm{V}}_{\mathrm{B}}^{-}$$ V B − excitation. This process is compatible with interlayer energy transfer while maintaining minimal electronic and spin hybridization and preserving optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) contrast. The heterostructure further exhibits improved sensitivity to external magnetic fields. These results establish a route for the enhancement of defect emission via interlayer optical coupling and introduce a general materials strategy for amplifying weak quantum defect signals in nanomaterials.

articles.title: Attribution of Changes in European Flood and Drought Magnitudes to Climatic and Socioeconomic Drivers
articles.titleEn: Attribution of Changes in European Flood and Drought Magnitudes to Climatic and Socioeconomic Drivers
articles.abstract: Hydrological extremes display long‐term trends and natural oscillations in response to climatic and socioeconomic factors. Knowing how and why these extremes are shifting is crucial for increasing water resilience in Europe. This work analyses trends in floods and droughts in European catchments between 1951 and 2020. Using the OS LISFLOOD hydrological model and non‐stationary extreme value analysis, we disentangle the effects of dynamics in climate, encompassing climate variability and climate change, land use, water abstraction and reservoirs on river flow extremes. Our results reveal spatial and temporal variations in magnitude of hydrological extremes. Land use changes have generally increased flood and drought hazards, while water demand primarily intensified droughts. Reservoirs, conversely, have decelerated the hydrological cycle. Our work delivers insights into the intricate connections between climate, society, and water in European river basins, enabling the development of effective strategies for enhancing resilience to extreme water events under global change.

articles.title: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
articles.titleEn: Cold activates a BH2 metabolic network promoting longevity and proteostasis
articles.abstract: Moderately cold temperatures extend lifespan and promote health across species 1–3 , yet the molecular mechanisms underlying these benefits remain unclear. Here we define a metabolite-driven, multi-tissue signalling system that links cold temperature to enhanced longevity and proteostasis in Caenorhabditis elegans . Cold temperature upregulates the biopterin-synthesis enzyme CAT-4 (GCH1 in humans), increasing production of dihydrobiopterin (BH2), a transportable reservoir for the bioactive cofactor tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4). BH2 is produced in muscle and transported to distal tissues, including the intestine and neurons, where it is converted into BH4 by the salvage enzyme DHFR-1. BH4 functions as an essential cofactor for phenylalanine hydroxylase PAH-1, promoting tyrosine synthesis and extending lifespan. This BH2–BH4 axis also prevents disease-related protein aggregation and subsequent neuronal dysfunction during ageing. Importantly, increasing BH2 synthesis specifically in muscle is sufficient to promote longevity and suppress pathological protein aggregation in distal tissues, even at normal or elevated temperatures. In human cells, BH2 or tyrosine supplementation reduces aggregation of polyQ-expanded proteins associated with Huntington’s disease, as well as mutant variants of TDP-43 and FUS that cause amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. Together, these findings identify BH2 as a cold-induced metabolite of which the synthesis, intertissue transport and conversion into bioactive BH4 preserve organism-wide proteostasis and extend lifespan.

articles.title: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
articles.titleEn: Drought and disease trigger novel interactions among top predators
articles.abstract: Interactions among species are increasingly recognized as key determinants of climate change impacts on ecosystems 1–5 . However, we know little about how climatic perturbations affect interactions among top vertebrate predators. Here we show that, when an emergent disease caused the decline of shared prey (rabbits), after decades of neutral co-existence a mammalian carnivore (lynx) started to prey heavily on a top predatory raptor (kites). These predation bouts occurred exclusively under drought conditions and when lynx found rabbit remains under the raptor nests, consistent with the removal of a potential competitor. Drought-induced lynx predation depressed lifetime reproductive success and triggered territory abandonment and dispersal by the raptor, suggestive of a new arms race among predators. A reduction in raptor abundance was associated with an increase in an insectivorous bird (a small owl), showing that the new interaction had the potential to reach lower trophic levels. These results underline the importance of diet flexibility and mobility as important mediators of resilience to stressors. In the future, synergistic effects of multiple anthropogenic stressors may reshape the interactions and ecological roles of many apex predators, with potential cascading consequences for whole ecosystems. A key to forecasting the future impact of global change may reside in understanding how behavioural flexibility and interacting keystone species respond to interacting shocks.

articles.title: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
articles.titleEn: Amazon carbon emissions driven by human actions amplified by droughts
articles.abstract: The Amazon carbon sink is weakening as deforestation 1–5 , rising tree mortality 6–8 and climate change disrupt the climatic conditions that sustain a humid tropical forest 9–11 . Forest loss reduces precipitation, increases temperatures and lengthens the dry season, driving higher carbon emissions 1–4,11,12 . Climate stress is stronger in more deforested regions, rendering forests progressively more flammable 1,9,13 . Large-scale climate events, such as El Niño, further amplify regional climate impacts 9,14–17 . Here we present an analysis of 15 years of Amazonian carbon fluxes derived from atmospheric CO 2 measurements. We determine a carbon balance of 0.32 ± 0.08 PgC yr −1 , with fires acting as the dominant source (0.40 ± 0.07 PgC yr −1 ) and forest uptake becoming increasingly unable to offset emissions. Furthermore, we investigate key drivers of the carbon emissions of Amazonia and identify three distinct year groups. Group 1 (2011–2014, 2017 and 2018) represents the role of the Amazon in the global carbon balance (0.11 ± 0.08 PgC yr −1 ) during wetter years with low human activity, such as deforestation, biomass burning and degradation. Group 2 (2019–2022) represents Amazon carbon emissions (0.43 ± 0.13 PgC yr −1 ) from human activities (mainly deforestation and degradation) during years with low climatic stress. Group 3 (2010, 2015, 2016, 2023 and 2024) has the highest carbon emissions (0.49 ± 0.07 PgC yr −1 ) and comprises warm and dry years (high climate stress), such as El Niño and the warming of the Tropical North Atlantic Ocean, associated with biomass burning.

articles.title: Enhancing simulations of disordered protein ensembles with chemical shift restraints in coarse-grained models
articles.titleEn: Enhancing simulations of disordered protein ensembles with chemical shift restraints in coarse-grained models
articles.abstract: With more than one third of the human proteome being structurally disordered, intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs) are key contributors to complex cellular functions, despite their highly dynamic conformational ensembles remaining elusive to conventional techniques in structural biology. Coarse-grained (CG) simulation methods thus serve as a gold standard to refine IDP ensembles. These methods, when relying on elastic network models or rigid body to sample secondary structure, are however inherently limited in their capability to model and sample transient secondary structure at a residue-level resolution as informed by experimental data. This fundamental limitation persists despite experimental evidence suggesting that transient structural propensities are a fundamental hallmark of IDP function. Through an artificial neural network capable of predicting backbone chemical shifts from C α -only protein conformations, we present a generalized framework which does not rely on dihedral parameterization to equip one bead-per-aminoacid CG force fields with the ability to sample functional elements of secondary structure. When applied on a large set of IDPs in isolation or condensates, our approach correctly recapitulates both local and global arrangements, yielding experimentally informed ensembles that can inform structure-mediated function and resolve force field limitations. This can yield a fruitful exploration of ensemble-to-function relationships in IDPs, allowing to explore phenomena such as secondary structure propensity and nucleation in condensates, conformationally selected binding motifs across disordered ensembles or conformational preferences of sequence-specific short-linear motifs.

articles.title: C1ql2 gates stress vulnerability by regulating microglia-mediated synaptic pruning in the BLA-vHPC circuit
articles.titleEn: C1ql2 gates stress vulnerability by regulating microglia-mediated synaptic pruning in the BLA-vHPC circuit
articles.abstract: Synaptic remodeling in emotional circuits contributes to the development of stress-related emotional disorders. However, such remodeling generally exhibits considerable heterogeneity across specific neuronal populations and the underlying molecular mechanisms remain poorly understood. Here, we identified C1ql2 as a key molecular regulator that governs projection-specific synaptic vulnerability within basolateral amygdala (BLA). Transcriptional profiling revealed that C1ql2 expression is enriched in BLA neurons projecting to ventral hippocampus (BLA →vHPC PNs), but not in those projecting to nucleus accumbens (NAc), and is significantly down-regulated following chronic social defeat stress (CSDS). Gain- and loss-of-function manipulations demonstrated that C1ql2 regulates stress-induced neuronal remodeling in BLA →vHPC PNs, including dendritic hypertrophy, synaptic outgrowth, and enhanced glutamatergic transmission, thereby shaping susceptibility to anxiety-like behavior. We further found that CSDS-induced C1ql2 loss impairs microglial engulfment of BLA →vHPC PNs synapses, leading to aberrant synaptic accumulation. Our findings establish C1ql2-mediated neuron-microglia cross talk that critically regulates circuit-specific synaptic pathophysiology in stress-related disorders.

articles.title: Anomalous narrow-band correlation in a natural superconducting heterostructure
articles.titleEn: Anomalous narrow-band correlation in a natural superconducting heterostructure
articles.abstract: A new frontier in condensed matter physics is to stack atomically thin layered materials with different properties and create intriguing phenomena which do not exist in any of the constituent layers. Transition metal dichalcogenide 4Hb-TaS 2, with an alternating stacking of a spin liquid candidate 1T-TaS 2 and a superconductor 1H-TaS 2 , is a natural heterostructure for such a purpose. Recently, rare phenomena were indeed observed, including chiral superconductivity, two-component nematic superconductivity, topological surface superconductivity, and enigmatic magnetic memory. A widely proposed starting point to understand such a mysterious heterostructure requires strong electronic correlation, presumably provided by 1T-TaS 2 layers with a narrow flat band near the Fermi level (E F ). Here, by using angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, we reveal the theoretically expected flat band near E F in the energy-momentum space. However, this flat band only exists on the 1T-TaS 2 terminated surface layer with broken translational symmetry, but not on the 1T-TaS 2 subsurface layers buried in the bulk. These results directly challenge the foundation of the current theoretical paradigm. On the 1T-TaS 2 terminated surface layer, we further revealed a pseudogap and an anomalous doping effect. These phenomena and the dichotomy between surface and bulk layers also shed light on the unusual coexistence of distinct electronic orders in this mysterious heterostructure.

articles.title: In-cloud motions shape warm-rain production in marine clouds: Evidence from multiyear observations
articles.titleEn: In-cloud motions shape warm-rain production in marine clouds: Evidence from multiyear observations
articles.abstract: Despite years of research, the processes controlling warm-rain formation remain uncertain. Leveraging multiple years of observations collected across four oceanic regions, we systematically reassess the properties of precipitation just beneath cloud base. The observations show that warm-rain characteristics are remarkably consistent within cloud regimes yet differ substantially between stratocumulus and cumulus, indicating that cloud-regime properties exert a stronger influence on warm precipitation than regional environmental variability. Precipitation is observed beneath marine stratocumulus in over 56% of cloudy columns with liquid water path (LWP) −2 , rising to more than 84% in columns with LWP beyond 130 g m −2 . This indicates that marine stratocumulus routinely support warm-rain formation and suggests that barriers to precipitation onset in this regime are weaker than commonly assumed. For the same LWP, oceanic cumulus precipitate less frequently than stratocumulus but on average produce two times larger and one to two orders of magnitude fewer precipitation drops. This contrast is consistent with cumulus presenting two times stronger updrafts and lower adiabaticity than stratocumulus, both of which can affect drop growth histories. Whereas the precipitation characteristics of stratocumulus are generally consistent with growth by collision–coalescence during gravitational free fall in low LWP clouds, those of cumulus cannot be explained without invoking additional processes. Together, these findings suggest that warm-precipitation parameterizations should more explicitly account for the influence of small-scale dynamical processes on precipitation growth. The apparent importance of drop growth histories further motivates continued exploration of Lagrangian particle-tracking approaches in both models and observations.

articles.title: Unveiling the structure of Leishmania flagella through cryoelectron tomography
articles.titleEn: Unveiling the structure of Leishmania flagella through cryoelectron tomography
articles.abstract: Leishmania are unicellular parasites that cause the serious disease leishmaniasis, presenting ongoing global challenges as existing treatments face issues with resistance and toxicity. Leishmania contain a single motile flagellum, essential for transmission, which has the conserved [9 + 2] microtubule arrangement. We used cryoelectron tomography to determine the ultrastructure of the Leishmania tarentolae 96-nm repeat and paraflagellar rod. While the overall structure, including three broad radial spokes and two-headed outer dynein arms, resembles other eukaryotes like Trypanosoma brucei, Tetrahymena, and Opisthokonts, the Leishmania flagellum also exhibits unique and asymmetrical features. These include asymmetrically shaped radial spoke heads similar to T. brucei , suggesting this may represent a kinetoplastid-specific feature. Further, Leishmania contain an additional inner-junction and 8-nm wide A2 protofilament hole. Strikingly, Leishmania have many doublet-specific structures such as outer dynein arm tethers, interdoublet linkers, and heterogeneous connections to the paraflagellar rod. In this work, we show that divergent structural traits of Leishmania flagella highlight lineage-specific adaptations within eukaryotes.

articles.title: Compensation of the effects of temperature on a motor system in the crab, Cancer borealis
articles.titleEn: Compensation of the effects of temperature on a motor system in the crab, Cancer borealis
articles.abstract: Understanding how warming affects life-critical physiological processes is increasingly important as ocean temperatures rise at unprecedented rates. We study the stomatogastric system of the crab Cancer borealis . Movement depends on multiple temperature-sensitive processes, from motor pattern generation to neuromuscular transmission and contraction. Previous studies examined these levels separately and showed that warming increased pyloric rhythm frequency until the rhythm crashed at extreme temperatures. Here, we examined how the neuromuscular transform responds to this increase in motor neuron activity. We simultaneously recorded motor neuron activity, muscle fiber membrane potential, and contraction force. As temperature increased, the pyloric rhythm frequency increased, the excitatory junctional potential amplitudes remained constant, and muscle contraction diminished and failed. When muscles were stimulated at a fixed low frequency mimicking neuronal activity at cold temperatures, contraction decreased with acute warming. Increasing motor nerve stimulation frequency to mimic neuronal activity at warm temperatures partially rescued contraction. Thus, a variety of temperature-dependent compensatory mechanisms overlap to extend the temperature range over which the neuromuscular system remains functional over a broad temperature range.

articles.title: Mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation driven by energetic-particle irradiation of icy solids
articles.titleEn: Mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation driven by energetic-particle irradiation of icy solids
articles.abstract: Mass-independent isotope fractionation (MIF) of oxygen provides key insights into atmospheric chemistry and the origin of isotopic anomalies in planetary materials. To date, MIF has been primarily associated with gas-phase processes involving symmetry-dependent reaction pathways, most notably ozone formation. Whether analogous effects can arise in condensed phases or at interfaces remains an open question. Here we report laboratory experiments demonstrating that energetic particle irradiation of icy oxide surfaces produces mass-independent oxygen isotope fractionation at temperatures as low as 10 K. Electron irradiation of SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 substrates in the presence of H 2 O ice results in measurable shifts in Δ 17 O in the underlying solids. The resulting three-isotope relationships include slope-1-like behavior in SiO 2 and Al 2 O 3 and distinct, substrate-dependent trends in Al 2 O 3 , indicating that irradiation-induced defect formation and interfacial chemistry govern the isotope effects. The magnitude of the observed anomalies demonstrates that irradiation-driven processes can generate substantial oxygen isotope heterogeneity in condensed phases. These results identify a previously unrecognized class of MIF and provide a quantitative framework for interpreting oxygen isotope signatures in radiation-processed environments, including interstellar grains and early solar system materials.

articles.title: A National Scale Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Enhanced Groundwater Depth Estimation
articles.titleEn: A National Scale Hybrid Machine Learning Model for Enhanced Groundwater Depth Estimation
articles.abstract: Groundwater is one of the most valuable natural resources, yet it is increasingly under pressure from climate change and human activities. Shallow groundwater depth (GWD) is a key indicator for evaluating groundwater availability and flood hazards, yet the measurements are often too sparse to capture its variability both in time and space. In this study, we evaluated hybrid data‐driven machine learning (ML) models that combine the strengths of existing hydrological simulations with the predictive power of ML methods for improved GWD estimation in Denmark. The hybrid model reduced mean bias of hydrological simulations from 1.72 to 0.22 m and decreased the Root Mean Square Error by about 1.64 m at national scale. Furthermore, we demonstrated that increasing the availability of GWD observations over time and space enhances model performance. We also illustrated the flexibility and effectiveness of the hybrid approach for GWD estimation across scales, and results showed that the hybrid model developed with coarse spatial resolutions can be easily used for high‐resolution GWD estimation without significant decrease of accuracy. This study highlights the potential of hybrid modeling as a practical solution for improving groundwater quantification accuracy and shows avenues for higher‐resolution estimates.

articles.title: Climatology and trends of observed daily and hourly extreme precipitation in the French Alps
articles.titleEn: Climatology and trends of observed daily and hourly extreme precipitation in the French Alps
articles.abstract: The French Alps, characterised by complex topography and diverse climatic influences, are highly vulnerable to extreme precipitation events, which can trigger floods and landslides with significant socio-economic impacts. While local stakeholders report a perceived increase in sub-daily extreme precipitation events, such a trend has not yet been statistically confirmed based on observations. In this study, we apply extreme value theory to long time series of in situ observations of daily and hourly precipitation to provide an updated climatology and trend analysis of precipitation extremes across the region. We focus on 20-year return levels to analyse rare, potentially high-impact events and show that precipitation extremes exhibit distinct spatial patterns with marked differences between daily and hourly timescales. By examining trends at monthly and seasonal levels and making use of an existing weather pattern classification, we gain a deeper understanding of the dynamics underlying these trends. For extremes of daily precipitation intensity, we observe strong positive trends in the southern French Alps and negative trends in the north, primarily driven by a stronger influence of southerly (Mediterranean) flows in autumn. The spatial patterns for hourly extremes show more spatially variable trends, and seem to be primarily influenced by local thermodynamic effects potentially linked to e.g. changing moisture availability or changes in surface albedo due to shorter snow cover persistence. This detailed analysis provides important insights for stakeholders who are working on prevention and protection from precipitation-related hazards, underscoring the need for adaptive strategies in response to changing precipitation patterns. It also highlights the importance of region-specific and timescale-specific approaches in future studies of precipitation extremes.

articles.title: HTAP3-OPNS: ozone, PM, nitrogen and sulphur deposition – multi-model experiments to support the revision of the CLRTAP Gothenburg Protocol
articles.titleEn: HTAP3-OPNS: ozone, PM, nitrogen and sulphur deposition – multi-model experiments to support the revision of the CLRTAP Gothenburg Protocol
articles.abstract: HTAP3-OPNS is a multi-model exercise designed to support the revision of the Gothenburg Protocol under the UNECE Convention on Long-Range Transboundary Air Pollution (CLRTAP). Using an ensemble of Chemical Transport Models (CTMs) and Chemistry-Climate Models (CCMs), this study investigates the long-range transport and impacts of ground-level ozone, particulate matter (PM), and nitrogen and sulphur deposition across different global regions. The project aims to assess the contributions of regional versus extra-regional emission sources, evaluate the suitability of current models, and project changes in air pollution under future emission scenarios and climate conditions. A series of perturbation simulations will enable the development of an ensemble emulator to explore and evaluate potential mitigation strategies efficiently. This paper outlines the scientific and policy questions motivating the study, describes the experimental design, including input datasets, model configurations, and required outputs, and discusses methodologies for data handling and analysis. The results will provide crucial insights for policy decisions aiming to improve air quality, protect human health, and protect ecosystems worldwide.

articles.title: A preliminary study on a synergistic assimilation scheme for multi-band satellite soil moisture data
articles.titleEn: A preliminary study on a synergistic assimilation scheme for multi-band satellite soil moisture data
articles.abstract: Soil moisture retrievals from satellite sensors operating at different microwave frequencies provide diverse and complementary data sources for assimilation. However, fully exploiting the advantages of each frequency band while increasing the volume of assimilated observations remains a challenge. This study assimilates soil-moisture retrievals from three dominant-frequency instruments – SMAP (Soil Moisture Active–Passive), ASCAT (Advanced Scatterometer), and MWRI (Microwave Radiation Imager) – into the Common Land Model (CoLM) via the Simplified Extended Kalman Filter (SEKF). Based on the systematic assessment of the disparate impacts of each single-band product, we propose and test a synergistic multi-satellite assimilation framework that optimally combines the complementary information inherent in the multi-frequency observations. Results show that assimilating soil-moisture retrievals improves the accuracy of the CoLM land-surface model; nevertheless, the effectiveness of each product varies with vegetation type. Analyses of simultaneous multi-source assimilation indicate that retrieval uncertainties associated with frequency-dependent differences in vegetation penetration capability are the dominant factor controlling the effectiveness of joint assimilation. When SMAP and ASCAT products are already ingested, the additional introduction of MWRI data over low-stature vegetation, where vegetation attenuation is relatively weak, provides complementary information and further enhances the joint assimilation performance. Validation against in-situ observations across China demonstrates that the largest improvements occur in the central and western parts of the country: compared with the open-loop simulation, the domain-mean correlation coefficient rises by about 0.25, while the error declines from 0.068 to 0.058 m 3 m −3 . This indicates that improvements from multi-sensor assimilation stem not only from increased data volume but also from the complementary characteristics of the assimilated products. These findings provide valuable insights into the design of synergistic multi-sensor land data assimilation systems and contribute to improving land surface modeling, as well as weather and climate prediction accuracy.

articles.title: A paired marine-fluvial modern pollen dataset from the Bohai Sea and its inflowing rivers, China
articles.titleEn: A paired marine-fluvial modern pollen dataset from the Bohai Sea and its inflowing rivers, China
articles.abstract: Modern marine pollen records can be interpreted reliably only when the main source-to-sink processes between terrestrial vegetation, rivers, and marine depocentres are documented by comparable modern data. Here, we present and quality-assess a paired marine-fluvial pollen dataset for the Bohai Sea, China, consisting of 430 marine surface-sediment samples and 104 fluvial surface-sediment samples from 16 major inflowing rivers. The dataset includes sample coordinates, water depth for marine stations, river and regional identifiers, pollen and spore counts and percentages, pollen concentrations, and grain-size parameters. In total, 104 pollen and spore morphotypes were identified. Marine assemblages are dominated by arboreal pollen, especially Pinus (mean 59 %), whereas nearshore and river-influenced settings contain higher proportions of herbaceous taxa, particularly Chenopodiaceae/Amaranthaceae-type (mean 14 %), Artemisia , and Poaceae. Redundancy analysis after variance-inflation-factor screening indicates that water depth is the strongest retained predictor of marine pollen composition (λ1/λ2=0.303), followed by geographic position and sediment texture. In river samples, geographic position, water discharge, and pollen concentration together explain 20.53 % of the compositional variance. Along the 0–35 m depth interval, arboreal pollen and Pinus percentages increase with water depth, whereas herbaceous percentages decrease, providing an internally consistent modern analogue for distinguishing nearshore fluvial influence from more distal marine influence, where buoyant saccate pollen is enriched by a combination of atmospheric transport and hydrodynamic sorting. The dataset is intended primarily as a reusable calibration and quality-assessment resource for palaeoenvironmental studies in the Bohai-Yellow Sea region. The archived data are available at the National Tibetan Plateau Data Center (TPDC; https://doi.org/10.11888/Paleoenv.tpdc.303516, Li and Yang, 2026).

articles.title: A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
articles.titleEn: A spatially resolved dataset of stable water isotopes in monthly precipitation over Jeju Island, Korea (2000–2003)
articles.abstract: Spatially resolved, multi-year observations of stable water isotopes in precipitation remain scarce for high-relief maritime islands. We present a historical dataset of monthly precipitation isotopes collected between September 2000 and December 2003 at 15 stations on Jeju Island, South Korea, spanning elevations of 5–1230 ma.s.l. The dataset contains 462 paired δ 18 O and δ 2 H measurements, deuterium excess ( d -excess = δ 2 H − 8 × δ 18 O), station and sampling metadata, and 488 station-month records of precipitation and air-temperature estimates, including 26 records without corresponding isotope measurements. Missing isotope observations were not imputed. Individual δ 18 O and δ 2 H values range from −13.2 ‰ to −2.0 ‰ and from −93.3 ‰ to −5.8 ‰, respectively, and generally exhibit lower values in summer than during the cool season. Unweighted station means for the common 2002–2003 period yield elevation gradients of −0.146 ± 0.013 ‰ per 100 m for δ 18 O and −1.043 ± 0.128 ‰ per 100 m for δ 2 H, with uncertainties expressed as standard errors. An island–nearshore comparison with isotope-enabled model output provides context for broad seasonal variability. By recovering and openly publishing observations collected more than two decades ago, this dataset preserves a historical baseline for subsequent precipitation-isotope monitoring and hydrological studies on Jeju Island. The data are available at https://doi.org/10.22747/paper_data.20260219.42 (Lee et al., 2026).
